steps.title: Find the relationship
steps.content: An analogy compares relationships, not just individual words. Identify the exact relationship in the first pair, then apply the same relationship to the second pair.
steps.example: Bird : Nest :: Bee : Hive. Both pairs are animal to home.

steps.title: Complete the analogy
steps.explanation: A doctor commonly works in a hospital; a teacher commonly works in a school.

steps.title: Recognize number analogies
steps.content: Number analogies may use addition, multiplication, squares, cubes or digit operations. Test a simple consistent rule on both numbers in the first pair.

steps.title: Find the odd one out
steps.explanation: 4, 9, 16 and 25 are perfect squares. 20 is not.

steps.title: State the grouping rule
steps.content: For odd-one-out questions, find a property shared by the majority and check that the exception truly breaks it. Avoid vague patterns that could fit several answers.
steps.tip: A good explanation names the rule and verifies every item.

questions.explanation: A glove is worn on a hand; a shoe is worn on a foot.
The first number is cubed: 2³=8 and 3³=27.
A book is read; food is eaten.
